label: Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Infections as: Invasion of the host organism by microorganisms or their toxins or by parasites that can cause pathological conditions or diseases.

label: Neoplasms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms as: New abnormal growth of tissue. Malignant neoplasms show a greater degree of anaplasia and have the properties of invasion and metastasis, compared to benign neoplasms.

label: Cardiovascular Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiovascular Diseases as: Pathological conditions involving the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM including the HEART ; the BLOOD VESSELS ; or the PERICARDIUM .

label: Nervous System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nervous System Diseases as: Diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. This includes disorders of the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, peripheral nerves, nerve roots, autonomic nervous system, neuromuscular junction, and muscle.

label: Respiratory Tract Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory Tract Diseases as: Diseases involving the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM .

label: Digestive System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Digestive System Diseases as: Diseases in any part of the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or the accessory organs ( LIVER ; BILIARY TRACT ; PANCREAS ).

label: Musculoskeletal Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Musculoskeletal Diseases as: Diseases of the muscles and their associated ligaments and other connective tissue and of the bones and cartilage viewed collectively.

label: Endocrine System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Endocrine System Diseases as: Pathological processes of the ENDOCRINE GLANDS , and diseases resulting from abnormal level of available HORMONES .

label: Immune System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Immune System Diseases as: Disorders caused by abnormal or absent immunologic mechanisms, whether humoral, cell-mediated, or both.

label: Mental Disorders
summary: NLM MeSH describes Mental Disorders as: Psychiatric illness or diseases manifested by breakdowns in the adaptational process expressed primarily as abnormalities of thought, feeling, and behavior producing either distress or impairment of function.

label: Wounds and Injuries
summary: NLM MeSH describes Wounds and Injuries as: Damage inflicted on the body as the direct or indirect result of an external force, with or without disruption of structural continuity.

label: Hemic and Lymphatic Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Hemic and Lymphatic Diseases as: Hematologic diseases and diseases of the lymphatic system collectively. Hemic diseases include disorders involving the formed elements (e.g., ERYTHROCYTE AGGREGATION, INTRAVASCULAR ) and chemical components (e.g., BLOOD PROTEIN DISORDERS ); lymphatic diseases include disorders relating to lymph, lymph nodes, and lymphocytes.

label: Aneurysm, Infected
summary: NLM MeSH describes Aneurysm, Infected as: Aneurysm due to growth of microorganisms in the arterial wall, or infection arising within preexisting arteriosclerotic aneurysms.

label: Arthritis, Infectious
summary: NLM MeSH describes Arthritis, Infectious as: Arthritis caused by BACTERIA ; RICKETTSIA ; MYCOPLASMA ; VIRUSES ; FUNGI ; or PARASITES .

label: Asymptomatic Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Asymptomatic Infections as: Infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

label: Bacterial Infections and Mycoses
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bacterial Infections and Mycoses as: Infections caused by bacteria and fungi, general, specified, or unspecified.

label: Bone Diseases, Infectious
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bone Diseases, Infectious as: Bone diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms.

label: Breakthrough Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Breakthrough Infections as: Infections by the same infectious agent (e.g., virus, fungus) occurring during exposure to prophylaxis, vaccine and treatment.

label: Cardiovascular Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiovascular Infections as: Pathological conditions of the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM caused by infections.

label: Catheter-Related Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Catheter-Related Infections as: Infections resulting from the use of catheters. Proper aseptic technique, site of catheter placement, material composition, and virulence of the organism are all factors that can influence possible infection.

label: Central Nervous System Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Central Nervous System Infections as: Pathogenic infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges. DNA VIRUS INFECTIONS ; RNA VIRUS INFECTIONS ; BACTERIAL INFECTIONS ; MYCOPLASMA INFECTIONS ; SPIROCHAETALES INFECTIONS ; fungal infections; PROTOZOAN INFECTIONS ; HELMINTHIASIS ; and PRION DISEASES may involve the central nervous system as a primary or secondary process.

label: Coinfection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Coinfection as: Simultaneous infection of a host organism by two or more pathogens. In virology, coinfection commonly refers to simultaneous infection of a single cell by two or more different viruses.

label: Communicable Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Communicable Diseases as: An illness caused by an infectious agent or its toxins that occurs through the direct or indirect transmission of the infectious agent or its products from an infected individual or via an animal, vector or the inanimate environment to a susceptible animal or human host.

label: Community-Acquired Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Community-Acquired Infections as: Any infection acquired in the community, that is, contrasted with those acquired in a health care facility ( CROSS INFECTION ). An infection would be classified as community-acquired if the patient had not recently been in a health care facility or been in contact with someone who had been recently in a health care facility.

label: Cross Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cross Infection as: Any infection which a patient contracts in a health-care institution.

label: Eye Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Eye Infections as: Infection, moderate to severe, caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses, which occurs either on the external surface of the eye or intraocularly with probable inflammation, visual impairment, or blindness.

label: Focal Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Focal Infection as: An infection at a specific location that may spread to another region of the body.

label: Gingivitis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Gingivitis as: Inflammation of gum tissue ( GINGIVA ) without loss of connective tissue.

label: Hepatitis, Animal
summary: NLM MeSH describes Hepatitis, Animal as: INFLAMMATION of the LIVER in non-human animals.

label: Intraabdominal Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Intraabdominal Infections as: Infection within the PERITONEAL CAVITY. A frequent cause is an ANASTOMOTIC LEAK following surgery.

label: Laboratory Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Laboratory Infection as: Accidentally acquired infection in laboratory workers.

label: Latent Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Latent Infection as: Delayed infection of the host by a dormant or inactive pathogen.

label: Opportunistic Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Opportunistic Infections as: An infection caused by an organism which becomes pathogenic under certain conditions, e.g., during immunosuppression.

label: Parasitic Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Parasitic Diseases as: Infections or infestations with PARASITES . They are often contracted through contact with an intermediate vector, but may occur as the result of direct exposure.

label: Pelvic Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pelvic Infection as: Infection involving the tissues or organs in the PELVIS .

label: Persistent Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Persistent Infection as: Infection which lasts for a long period with continuous display of clinical features. Persistent infection arises due to inability of host cells to clear primary infections completely. When persistent infections are cleared so that infection symptoms are under control they are often referred to as chronic infections. LATENT INFECTIONS are infections in which manifestation of clinical symptoms appear later.

label: Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome
summary: NLM MeSH describes Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome as: An acute, transmissible, infectious disease associated with high MORTALITY and MORBIDITY in young turkeys (poults). It is characterized by DIARRHEA ; ANOREXIA ; growth depression, and immune dysfunction. The cause is unknown but astroviruses ( AVASTROVIRUS ) and coronaviruses ( CORONAVIRUS, TURKEY ) have been isolated from diseased poults and are thought to cause the enteritis and increased susceptibility to bacterial infections.

label: Pregnancy Complications, Infectious
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pregnancy Complications, Infectious as: The co-occurrence of pregnancy and an INFECTION . The infection may precede or follow FERTILIZATION .

label: Prosthesis-Related Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Prosthesis-Related Infections as: Infections resulting from the implantation of prosthetic devices. The infections may be acquired from intraoperative contamination (early) or hematogenously acquired from other sites (late).

label: Reproductive Tract Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Reproductive Tract Infections as: Infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

label: Respiratory Tract Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory Tract Infections as: Invasion of the host RESPIRATORY SYSTEM by microorganisms, usually leading to pathological processes or diseases.

label: Sepsis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sepsis as: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome with a proven or suspected infectious etiology. When sepsis is associated with organ dysfunction distant from the site of infection, it is called severe sepsis. When sepsis is accompanied by HYPOTENSION despite adequate fluid infusion, it is called SEPTIC SHOCK .

label: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sexually Transmitted Diseases as: Diseases due to or propagated by sexual contact.

label: Skin Diseases, Infectious
summary: NLM MeSH describes Skin Diseases, Infectious as: Skin diseases caused by bacteria, fungi, parasites, or viruses.

label: Soft Tissue Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Soft Tissue Infections as: Infections of non-skeletal tissue, i.e., exclusive of bone, ligaments, cartilage, and fibrous tissue. The concept is usually referred to as skin and soft tissue infections and usually subcutaneous and muscle tissue are involved. The predisposing factors in anaerobic infections are trauma, ischemia, and surgery. The organisms often derive from the fecal or oral flora, particularly in wounds associated with intestinal surgery, decubitus ulcer, and human bites. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p1688)

label: Suppuration
summary: NLM MeSH describes Suppuration as: A pathologic process consisting in the formation of pus.

label: Toxemia
summary: NLM MeSH describes Toxemia as: A condition produced by the presence of toxins or other harmful substances in the BLOOD .

label: Urinary Tract Infections
summary: NLM MeSH describes Urinary Tract Infections as: Inflammatory responses of the epithelium of the URINARY TRACT to microbial invasions. They are often bacterial infections with associated BACTERIURIA and PYURIA .

label: Vaccine-Preventable Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Vaccine-Preventable Diseases as: Diseases for which vaccines exist that can confer partial or complete protection. (World Health Organization vaccine-safety-training.org)

label: Vector Borne Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Vector Borne Diseases as: Infectious diseases transmitted by DISEASE VECTORS .

label: Virus Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Virus Diseases as: A general term for diseases caused by viruses.

label: Waterborne Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Waterborne Diseases as: Illnesses due to micro-organisms and chemicals in drinking water, those caused by organisms having part of their lifecycle in water or those with water-related vectors, and others spread by aerosols containing pathogens.

label: Wound Infection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Wound Infection as: Invasion of a wound by pathogenic microorganisms.

label: Zoonoses
summary: NLM MeSH describes Zoonoses as: Diseases of non-human animals that may be transmitted to HUMANS or may be transmitted from humans to non-human animals.

label: Cysts
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cysts as: Any fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an EPITHELIUM . Cysts can be of normal, abnormal, non-neoplastic, or neoplastic tissues.

label: Hamartoma
summary: NLM MeSH describes Hamartoma as: A focal malformation resembling a neoplasm, composed of an overgrowth of mature cells and tissues that normally occur in the affected area.

label: Neoplasms by Histologic Type
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms by Histologic Type as: A collective term for the various histological types of NEOPLASMS . It is more likely to be used by searchers than by indexers and catalogers.

label: Neoplasms by Site
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms by Site as: A collective term for precoordinated organ/neoplasm headings locating neoplasms by organ, as BRAIN NEOPLASMS ; DUODENAL NEOPLASMS ; LIVER NEOPLASMS ; etc.

label: Neoplasms, Experimental
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Experimental as: Experimentally induced new abnormal growth of TISSUES in animals to provide models for studying human neoplasms.

label: Neoplasms, Hormone-Dependent
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Hormone-Dependent as: Certain tumors that 1, arise in organs that are normally dependent on specific hormones and 2, are stimulated or caused to regress by manipulation of the endocrine environment.

label: Neoplasms, Multiple Primary
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Multiple Primary as: Two or more abnormal growths of tissue occurring simultaneously and presumed to be of separate origin. The neoplasms may be histologically the same or different, and may be found in the same or different sites.

label: Neoplasms, Post-Traumatic
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Post-Traumatic as: Tumors, cancer or other neoplasms caused by or resulting from trauma or other non-radiation injuries.

label: Neoplasms, Radiation-Induced
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Radiation-Induced as: Tumors, cancer or other neoplasms produced by exposure to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation.

label: Neoplasms, Second Primary
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms, Second Primary as: Abnormal growths of tissue that follow a previous neoplasm but are not metastases of the latter. The second neoplasm may have the same or different histological type and can occur in the same or different organs as the previous neoplasm but in all cases arises from an independent oncogenic event. The development of the second neoplasm may or may not be related to the treatment for the previous neoplasm since genetic risk or predisposing factors may actually be the cause.

label: Neoplastic Processes
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplastic Processes as: The pathological mechanisms and forms taken by tissue during degeneration into a neoplasm and its subsequent activity.

label: Neoplastic Syndromes, Hereditary
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplastic Syndromes, Hereditary as: The condition of a pattern of malignancies within a family, but not every individual's necessarily having the same neoplasm. Characteristically the tumor tends to occur at an earlier than average age, individuals may have more than one primary tumor, the tumors may be multicentric, usually more than 25 percent of the individuals in direct lineal descent from the proband are affected, and the cancer predisposition in these families behaves as an autosomal dominant trait with about 60 percent penetrance.

label: Paraneoplastic Syndromes
summary: NLM MeSH describes Paraneoplastic Syndromes as: In patients with neoplastic diseases a wide variety of clinical pictures which are indirect and usually remote effects produced by tumor cell metabolites or other products.

label: Precancerous Conditions
summary: NLM MeSH describes Precancerous Conditions as: Pathological conditions that tend eventually to become malignant.

label: Pregnancy Complications, Neoplastic
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pregnancy Complications, Neoplastic as: The co-occurrence of pregnancy and NEOPLASMS . The neoplastic disease may precede or follow FERTILIZATION .

label: Cardiovascular Abnormalities
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiovascular Abnormalities as: Congenital, inherited, or acquired anomalies of the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM , including the HEART and BLOOD VESSELS .

label: Heart Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Heart Diseases as: Pathological conditions involving the HEART including its structural and functional abnormalities.

label: Pregnancy Complications, Cardiovascular
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pregnancy Complications, Cardiovascular as: The co-occurrence of pregnancy and a cardiovascular disease. The disease may precede or follow FERTILIZATION and it may or may not have a deleterious effect on the pregnant woman or FETUS .

label: Vascular Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Vascular Diseases as: Pathological processes involving any of the BLOOD VESSELS in the cardiac or peripheral circulation. They include diseases of ARTERIES ; VEINS ; and rest of the vasculature system in the body.

label: Autoimmune Diseases of the Nervous System
summary: NLM MeSH describes Autoimmune Diseases of the Nervous System as: Disorders caused by cellular or humoral immune responses primarily directed towards nervous system autoantigens. The immune response may be directed towards specific tissue components (e.g., myelin) and may be limited to the central nervous system (e.g., MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS ) or the peripheral nervous system (e.g., GUILLAIN-BARRE SYNDROME ).

label: Autonomic Nervous System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Autonomic Nervous System Diseases as: Diseases of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM , including sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric nervous systems.

label: Central Nervous System Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Central Nervous System Diseases as: Diseases of any component of the brain (including the cerebral hemispheres, diencephalon, brain stem, and cerebellum) or the spinal cord.

label: Chronobiology Disorders
summary: NLM MeSH describes Chronobiology Disorders as: Disruptions of the rhythmic cycle of bodily functions or activities.

label: Cranial Nerve Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Cranial Nerve Diseases as: Disorders of one or more of the twelve cranial nerves. With the exception of the optic and olfactory nerves, this includes disorders of the brain stem nuclei from which the cranial nerves originate or terminate.

label: Demyelinating Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Demyelinating Diseases as: Diseases characterized by loss or dysfunction of myelin in the central or peripheral nervous system.

label: Nervous System Malformations
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nervous System Malformations as: Structural abnormalities of the central or peripheral nervous system resulting primarily from defects of embryogenesis.

label: Nervous System Neoplasms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nervous System Neoplasms as: Benign and malignant neoplastic processes arising from or involving components of the central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous systems, cranial nerves, and meninges. Included in this category are primary and metastatic nervous system neoplasms.

label: Neurocutaneous Syndromes
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurocutaneous Syndromes as: A group of disorders characterized by ectodermal-based malformations and neoplastic growths in the skin, nervous system, and other organs.

label: Neurodegenerative Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurodegenerative Diseases as: Hereditary and sporadic conditions which are characterized by progressive nervous system dysfunction. These disorders are often associated with atrophy of the affected central or peripheral nervous system structures.

label: Neuroinflammatory Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neuroinflammatory Diseases as: Diseases characterized by inflammation of the nervous tissue.

label: Neurologic Manifestations
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurologic Manifestations as: Clinical signs and symptoms caused by nervous system injury or dysfunction.

label: Neuromuscular Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neuromuscular Diseases as: A general term encompassing lower MOTOR NEURON DISEASE ; PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASES ; and certain MUSCULAR DISEASES . Manifestations include MUSCLE WEAKNESS ; FASCICULATION ; muscle ATROPHY ; SPASM ; MYOKYMIA ; MUSCLE HYPERTONIA , myalgias, and MUSCLE HYPOTONIA .

label: Neurotoxicity Syndromes
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurotoxicity Syndromes as: Neurologic disorders caused by exposure to toxic substances through ingestion, injection, cutaneous application, or other method. This includes conditions caused by biologic, chemical, and pharmaceutical agents.

label: Restless Legs Syndrome
summary: NLM MeSH describes Restless Legs Syndrome as: A disorder characterized by aching or burning sensations in the lower and rarely the upper extremities that occur prior to sleep or may awaken the patient from sleep.

label: Sleep Wake Disorders
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sleep Wake Disorders as: Abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

label: Trauma, Nervous System
summary: NLM MeSH describes Trauma, Nervous System as: Traumatic injuries to the brain, cranial nerves, spinal cord, autonomic nervous system, or neuromuscular system, including iatrogenic injuries induced by surgical procedures.

label: Bronchial Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bronchial Diseases as: Diseases involving the BRONCHI .

label: Ciliary Motility Disorders
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ciliary Motility Disorders as: Conditions caused by abnormal CILIA movement in the body, usually causing KARTAGENER SYNDROME , chronic respiratory disorders, chronic SINUSITIS , and chronic OTITIS . Abnormal ciliary beating is likely due to defects in any of the 200 plus ciliary proteins, such as missing motor enzyme DYNEIN arms.

label: Granuloma, Respiratory Tract
summary: NLM MeSH describes Granuloma, Respiratory Tract as: Granulomatous disorders affecting one or more sites in the respiratory tract.

label: Laryngeal Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Laryngeal Diseases as: Pathological processes involving any part of the LARYNX which coordinates many functions such as voice production, breathing, swallowing, and coughing.

label: Lung Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Lung Diseases as: Pathological processes involving any part of the LUNG .

label: Nose Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Nose Diseases as: Disorders of the nose, general or unspecified.

label: Pleural Diseases
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pleural Diseases as: Diseases involving the PLEURA .

label: Respiration Disorders
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiration Disorders as: Diseases of the respiratory system in general or unspecified or for a specific respiratory disease not available.

label: Respiratory Hypersensitivity
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory Hypersensitivity as: A form of hypersensitivity affecting the respiratory tract. It includes ASTHMA and RHINITIS, ALLERGIC, SEASONAL .

label: Respiratory System Abnormalities
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory System Abnormalities as: Congenital structural abnormalities of the respiratory system.

label: Behavior and Behavior Mechanisms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavior and Behavior Mechanisms as: The observable response made to a situation and the unconscious processes underlying it.

label: Adaptation, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Adaptation, Psychological as: A state of harmony between internal needs and external demands and the processes used in achieving this condition. (From APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed).

label: Attitude
summary: NLM MeSH describes Attitude as: An enduring, learned predisposition to behave in a consistent way toward a given class of objects, or a persistent mental and/or neural state of readiness to react to a certain class of objects, not as they are but as they are conceived to be.

label: Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavior as: The observable response of a man or animal to a situation.

label: Child Rearing
summary: NLM MeSH describes Child Rearing as: The training or bringing-up of children by parents or parent-substitutes. It is used also for child rearing practices in different societies, at different economic levels, in different ethnic groups, etc. It differs from PARENTING in that in child rearing the emphasis is on the act of training or bringing up the child and the interaction between the parent and child, while parenting emphasizes the responsibility and qualities of exemplary behavior of the parent.

label: Defense Mechanisms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Defense Mechanisms as: Unconscious process used by an individual or a group of individuals in order to cope with impulses, feelings or ideas which are not acceptable at their conscious level; various types include reaction formation, projection and self reversal.

label: Emotions
summary: NLM MeSH describes Emotions as: Those affective states which can be experienced and have arousing and motivational properties.

label: Outcome Expectations
summary: NLM MeSH describes Outcome Expectations as: Believed or anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.

label: Human Characteristics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Human Characteristics as: The fundamental dispositions and traits of humans. (Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

label: Human Development
summary: NLM MeSH describes Human Development as: Continuous sequential changes which occur in the physiological and psychological functions during the life-time of an individual.

label: Mental Competency
summary: NLM MeSH describes Mental Competency as: The ability to understand the nature and effect of the act in which the individual is engaged. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 6th ed).

label: Motivation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Motivation as: Those factors which cause an organism to behave or act in either a goal-seeking or satisfying manner. They may be influenced by physiological drives or by external stimuli.

label: Neurobehavioral Manifestations
summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurobehavioral Manifestations as: Signs and symptoms of higher cortical dysfunction caused by organic conditions. These include certain behavioral alterations and impairments of skills involved in the acquisition, processing, and utilization of knowledge or information.

label: Personality
summary: NLM MeSH describes Personality as: Behavior-response patterns that characterize the individual.

label: Psychology, Social
summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychology, Social as: The branch of psychology concerned with the effects of group membership upon the behavior, attitudes, and beliefs of an individual.

label: Psychosocial Functioning
summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychosocial Functioning as: Level of and variations in social and emotional activity or behaviors.

label: Temperance
summary: NLM MeSH describes Temperance as: Habitual moderation in the indulgence of a natural appetite, especially but not exclusively the consumption of alcohol.

label: Coping Skills
summary: NLM MeSH describes Coping Skills as: Various techniques for actively managing a stressful event or situation.

label: Emotional Adjustment
summary: NLM MeSH describes Emotional Adjustment as: Psychological process that occurs when an individual adapts to a significant emotional event or stimulus.

label: Feedback, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Feedback, Psychological as: A mechanism of information stimulus and response that may control subsequent behavior, cognition, perception, or performance. (From APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

label: Orientation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Orientation as: Awareness of oneself in relation to time, place and person.

label: Posttraumatic Growth, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Posttraumatic Growth, Psychological as: Positive change experienced as a result of the struggle with a major life crisis or a traumatic event.

label: Psychological Growth
summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychological Growth as: A process of actively learning and adapting to new ways to function following a challenging life crisis.

label: Sense of Coherence
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sense of Coherence as: A view of the world and the individual's environment as comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful, claiming that the way people view their life has a positive influence on their health.

label: Attitude of Health Personnel
summary: NLM MeSH describes Attitude of Health Personnel as: Attitudes of personnel toward their patients, other professionals, toward the medical care system, etc.

label: Attitude to Computers
summary: NLM MeSH describes Attitude to Computers as: The attitude and behavior associated with an individual using the computer.

label: Attitude to Death
summary: NLM MeSH describes Attitude to Death as: Conceptual response of the person to the various aspects of death, which are based on individual psychosocial and cultural experience.

label: Attitude to Health
summary: NLM MeSH describes Attitude to Health as: Public attitudes toward health, disease, and the medical care system.

label: Catastrophization
summary: NLM MeSH describes Catastrophization as: Cognitive and emotional processes encompassing magnification of pain-related stimuli, feelings of helplessness, and a generally pessimistic orientation.

label: Optimism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Optimism as: Mental attitude that interprets life events as generally being positive.

label: Pessimism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Pessimism as: Mental attitude that interprets life events as generally being negative.

label: Respect
summary: NLM MeSH describes Respect as: A feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities, qualities, or achievements and regard for the feelings, wishes, or rights of others.

label: Stereotyping
summary: NLM MeSH describes Stereotyping as: An oversimplified perception or conception especially of persons, social groups, etc.

label: Accident Proneness
summary: NLM MeSH describes Accident Proneness as: Tendency toward involvement in accidents. Implies certain personality characteristics which predispose to accidents.

label: Adolescent Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Adolescent Behavior as: Any observable response or action of an adolescent.

label: Behavior, Animal
summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavior, Animal as: The observable response an animal makes to any situation.

label: Behavioral Symptoms
summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavioral Symptoms as: Observable manifestations of impaired psychological functioning.

label: Child Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Child Behavior as: Any observable response or action of a child from 24 months through 12 years of age. For neonates or children younger than 24 months, INFANT BEHAVIOR is available.

label: Codependency, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Codependency, Psychological as: A relational pattern in which a person attempts to derive a sense of purpose through relationships with others.

label: Communication
summary: NLM MeSH describes Communication as: The exchange or transmission of ideas, attitudes, or beliefs between individuals or groups.

label: Consumer Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Consumer Behavior as: Behavior associated with the procurement of goods, services, or experiences.

label: Criminal Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Criminal Behavior as: Conduct leading to commission of unlawful acts.

label: Dangerous Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Dangerous Behavior as: Actions which have a high risk of being harmful or injurious to oneself or others.

label: Drinking Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Drinking Behavior as: Behaviors associated with the ingesting of water and other liquids; includes rhythmic patterns of drinking (time intervals - onset and duration), frequency and satiety.

label: Drug-Seeking Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Drug-Seeking Behavior as: Activities performed to obtain licit or illicit substances.

label: Escape Reaction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Escape Reaction as: Innate response elicited by sensory stimuli associated with a threatening situation, or actual confrontation with an enemy.

label: Exploratory Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Exploratory Behavior as: The tendency to explore or investigate a novel environment. It is considered a motivation not clearly distinguishable from curiosity.

label: Feeding Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Feeding Behavior as: Behavioral responses or sequences associated with eating including modes of feeding, rhythmic patterns of eating, and time intervals.

label: Habits
summary: NLM MeSH describes Habits as: Acquired or learned responses which are regularly manifested.

label: Harm Reduction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Harm Reduction as: The application of methods designed to reduce the risk of harm associated with certain behaviors without reduction in frequency of those behaviors. The risk-associated behaviors include ongoing and active addictive behaviors.

label: Health Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Health Behavior as: Combination of HEALTH KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, PRACTICE which underlie actions taken by individuals regarding their health.

label: Hoarding
summary: NLM MeSH describes Hoarding as: A persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions.

label: Human-Animal Interaction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Human-Animal Interaction as: Encompasses any situation where there is interchange between human(s) and animal(s) at an individual or cultural level. These interactions are diverse and idiosyncratic, and may be fleeting or profound. (https://www.avma.org/KB/Policies/Pages/The-Human-Animal-Bond.aspx accessed 8/22/2019).

label: Illness Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Illness Behavior as: Coordinate set of non-specific behavioral responses to non-psychiatric illness. These may include loss of APPETITE or LIBIDO ; disinterest in ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING ; or withdrawal from social interaction.

label: Imitative Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Imitative Behavior as: The mimicking of the behavior of one individual by another.

label: Impulsive Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Impulsive Behavior as: An act performed without delay, reflection, voluntary direction or obvious control in response to a stimulus.

label: Information Seeking Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Information Seeking Behavior as: How information is gathered in personal, academic or work environments and the resources used.

label: Inhibition, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Inhibition, Psychological as: The interference with or prevention of a behavioral or verbal response even though the stimulus for that response is present; in psychoanalysis the unconscious restraining of an instinctual process.

label: Marijuana Use
summary: NLM MeSH describes Marijuana Use as: Medicinal or recreational utilization of MARIJUANA .

label: Motor Activity
summary: NLM MeSH describes Motor Activity as: Body movements of a human or an animal as a behavioral phenomenon.

label: Multitasking Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Multitasking Behavior as: Simultaneous task performance, or switching between tasks in a concentrated period of time.

label: Personal Satisfaction
summary: NLM MeSH describes Personal Satisfaction as: The individual's experience of a sense of fulfillment of a need or want and the quality or state of being satisfied.

label: Recreational Drug Use
summary: NLM MeSH describes Recreational Drug Use as: Occasional or habitual non-prescribed, not health-related use of substances.

label: Reproductive Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Reproductive Behavior as: Human behavior or decision related to REPRODUCTION .

label: Risk Reduction Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Risk Reduction Behavior as: Reduction of high-risk choices and adoption of low-risk quantity and frequency alternatives.

label: Risk-Taking
summary: NLM MeSH describes Risk-Taking as: Undertaking a task involving a challenge for achievement or a desirable goal in which there is a lack of certainty or a fear of failure. It may also include the exhibiting of certain behaviors whose outcomes may present a risk to the individual or to those associated with him or her.

label: Sedentary Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sedentary Behavior as: Behaviors during waking hours that have low energy expenditure and are often performed in a sitting or reclining POSTURE .

label: Self Stimulation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Self Stimulation as: The act or process of inducing or increasing the level of arousal in oneself. It can be observed in various situations; for example, infants who are understimulated may explore their surroundings or babble to themselves.(https://dictionary.apa.org/self-stimulation accessed 12/30/2020)

label: Sexual Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sexual Behavior as: Sexual activities of humans.

label: Smoking
summary: NLM MeSH describes Smoking as: Willful or deliberate act of inhaling and exhaling SMOKE from burning substances or agents held by hand.

label: Social Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Behavior as: Any behavior caused by or affecting another individual or group usually of the same species.

label: Spatial Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Spatial Behavior as: Reactions of an individual or groups of individuals with relation to the immediate surrounding area including the animate or inanimate objects within that area.

label: Stereotyped Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Stereotyped Behavior as: Relatively invariant mode of behavior elicited or determined by a particular situation; may be verbal, postural, or expressive.

label: Sucking Behavior
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sucking Behavior as: Any suction exerted by the mouth; response of the mammalian infant to draw milk from the breast. Includes sucking on inanimate objects. Not to be used for thumb sucking, which is indexed under fingersucking.

label: Tobacco Use
summary: NLM MeSH describes Tobacco Use as: Use of TOBACCO (Nicotiana tabacum L) and TOBACCO PRODUCTS .

label: Toilet Training
summary: NLM MeSH describes Toilet Training as: Conditioning to defecate and urinate in culturally acceptable places.

label: Acting Out
summary: NLM MeSH describes Acting Out as: Expressing unconscious emotional conflicts or feelings, often of hostility or love, through overt behavior.

label: Denial, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Denial, Psychological as: Refusal to admit the truth or reality of a situation or experience.

label: Displacement, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Displacement, Psychological as: The process by which an emotional or behavioral response that is appropriate for one situation appears in another situation for which it is inappropriate.

label: Fantasy
summary: NLM MeSH describes Fantasy as: An imagined sequence of events or mental images, e.g., daydreams.

label: Helplessness, Learned
summary: NLM MeSH describes Helplessness, Learned as: Learned expectation that one's responses are independent of reward and, hence, do not predict or control the occurrence of rewards. Learned helplessness derives from a history, experimentally induced or naturally occurring, of having received punishment/aversive stimulation regardless of responses made. Such circumstances result in an impaired ability to learn. Used for human or animal populations. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

label: Identification, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Identification, Psychological as: A process by which an individual unconsciously endeavors to pattern himself after another. This process is also important in the development of the personality, particularly the superego or conscience, which is modeled largely on the behavior of adult significant others.

label: Information Avoidance
summary: NLM MeSH describes Information Avoidance as: Choosing to not obtain knowledge even if having the information could be to one's benefit.

label: Perceptual Defense
summary: NLM MeSH describes Perceptual Defense as: Selective perceiving such that the individual protects himself from becoming aware of something unpleasant or threatening, e.g., obscene words are not heard correctly, or violent acts are not seen accurately.

label: Procrastination
summary: NLM MeSH describes Procrastination as: The deferment of actions or tasks to a later time, or to infinity.

label: Projection
summary: NLM MeSH describes Projection as: A defense mechanism, operating unconsciously, whereby that which is emotionally unacceptable in the self is rejected and attributed (projected) to others.

label: Rationalization
summary: NLM MeSH describes Rationalization as: A defense mechanism operating unconsciously, in which the individual attempts to justify or make consciously tolerable, by plausible means, feelings, behavior, and motives that would otherwise be intolerable.

label: Regression, Psychology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Regression, Psychology as: A return to earlier, especially to infantile, patterns of thought or behavior, or stage of functioning, e.g., feelings of helplessness and dependency in a patient with a serious physical illness. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994).

label: Repression, Psychology
summary: NLM MeSH describes Repression, Psychology as: The active mental process of keeping out and ejecting, banishing from consciousness, ideas or impulses that are unacceptable to it.

label: Sublimation, Psychological
summary: NLM MeSH describes Sublimation, Psychological as: A defense mechanism through which unacceptable impulses and instinctive urges are diverted into personally and socially acceptable channels; e.g., aggression may be diverted through sports activities.

label: Affect
summary: NLM MeSH describes Affect as: The feeling-tone accompaniment of an idea or mental representation. It is the most direct psychic derivative of instinct and the psychic representative of the various bodily changes by means of which instincts manifest themselves.

label: Anger
summary: NLM MeSH describes Anger as: A strong emotional feeling of displeasure aroused by being interfered with, injured or threatened.

label: Anxiety
summary: NLM MeSH describes Anxiety as: Feelings or emotions of dread, apprehension, and impending disaster but not disabling as with ANXIETY DISORDERS .

label: Apathy
summary: NLM MeSH describes Apathy as: Lack of emotion or emotional expression; a disorder of motivation that persists over time.

label: Bereavement
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bereavement as: Refers to the whole process of grieving and mourning and is associated with a deep sense of loss and sadness.

label: Boredom
summary: NLM MeSH describes Boredom as: A psychological state resulting from any activity that lacks motivation, or from enforced continuance in an uninteresting situation.

label: Courage
summary: NLM MeSH describes Courage as: State of mind or spirit that enables one to act in the face of perceived danger, difficulty, or pain.

label: Depression
summary: NLM MeSH describes Depression as: Depressive states usually of moderate intensity in contrast with MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER present in neurotic and psychotic disorders.

label: Disgust
summary: NLM MeSH describes Disgust as: A feeling of revulsion or strong disapproval aroused by something unpleasant or offensive.

label: Emotional Exhaustion
summary: NLM MeSH describes Emotional Exhaustion as: A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.

label: Bioethical Issues
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bioethical Issues as: Clusters of topics that fall within the domain of BIOETHICS , the field of study concerned with value questions that arise in biomedicine and health care delivery.

label: Bioethics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Bioethics as: A branch of applied ethics that studies the value implications of practices and developments in life sciences, medicine, and health care.

label: Codes of Ethics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Codes of Ethics as: Systematic statements of principles or rules of appropriate professional conduct, usually established by professional societies.

label: Complicity
summary: NLM MeSH describes Complicity as: Association with or participation in an act that is, or is perceived to be, criminal or immoral. One is complicitous when one promotes or unduly benefits from practices or institutions that are morally or legally suspect.

label: Conflict of Interest
summary: NLM MeSH describes Conflict of Interest as: A situation in which an individual might benefit personally from official or professional actions. It includes a conflict between a person's private interests and official responsibilities in a position of trust. The term is not restricted to government officials. The concept refers both to actual conflict of interest and the appearance or perception of conflict.

label: Double Effect Principle
summary: NLM MeSH describes Double Effect Principle as: Guideline for determining when it is morally permissible to perform an action to pursue a good end with knowledge that the action will also bring about bad results. It generally states that, in cases where a contemplated action has such double effect, the action is permissible only if: it is not wrong in itself; the bad result is not intended; the good result is not a direct causal result of the bad result; and the good result is proportionate to the bad result. (from Solomon, Double Effect, in Becker, The Encyclopedia of Ethics, 1992)

label: Ethical Analysis
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethical Analysis as: The use of systematic methods of ethical examination, such as CASUISTRY or ETHICAL THEORY , in reasoning about moral problems.

label: Ethical Relativism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethical Relativism as: The philosophical view that conceptions of truth and moral values are not absolute but are relative to the persons or groups holding them. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed)

label: Ethical Review
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethical Review as: A formal process of examination of patient care or research proposals for conformity with ethical standards. The review is usually conducted by an organized clinical or research ethics committee ( CLINICAL ETHICS COMMITTEES or RESEARCH ETHICS COMMITTEES ), sometimes by a subset of such a committee, an ad hoc group, or an individual ethicist ( ETHICISTS ).

label: Ethical Theory
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethical Theory as: A philosophically coherent set of propositions (for example, utilitarianism) which attempts to provide general norms for the guidance and evaluation of moral conduct. (from Beauchamp and Childress, Principles of Biomedical Ethics, 4th ed)

label: Ethics, Business
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Business as: The moral obligations governing the conduct of commercial or industrial enterprises.

label: Ethics, Institutional
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Institutional as: The moral and ethical obligations or responsibilities of institutions.

label: Ethics, Professional
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Professional as: The principles of proper conduct concerning the rights and duties of the professional, relations with patients or consumers and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the professional and interpersonal relations with patient or consumer families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

label: Ethics, Research
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Research as: The moral obligations governing the conduct of research. Used for discussions of research ethics as a general topic.

label: Humanism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Humanism as: An ethical system which emphasizes human values and the personal worth of each individual, as well as concern for the dignity and freedom of humankind.

label: Moral Status
summary: NLM MeSH describes Moral Status as: A philosophical description of intrinsic self-worth and dignity which bestows basic rights of life, liberty, and freedom from harm.

label: Personhood
summary: NLM MeSH describes Personhood as: The state or condition of being a human individual accorded moral and/or legal rights. Criteria to be used to determine this status are subject to debate, and range from the requirement of simply being a human organism to such requirements as that the individual be self-aware and capable of rational thought and moral agency.

label: Principle-Based Ethics
summary: NLM MeSH describes Principle-Based Ethics as: An approach to ethics that focuses on theories of the importance of general principles such as respect for autonomy, beneficence/nonmaleficence, and justice.

label: Symbolic Interactionism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Symbolic Interactionism as: Theoretical approach to social processes with a fundamental concern with power phenomena. There is a focus on the analysis of culture, the influence of Foucault, and the development of feminist perspectives.

label: Ethics, Clinical
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Clinical as: The identification, analysis, and resolution of moral problems that arise in the care of patients. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

label: Casuistry
summary: NLM MeSH describes Casuistry as: A method of ETHICAL ANALYSIS that emphasizes practical problem solving through examining individual cases that are considered to be representative; sometimes used to denote specious argument or rationalization. Differentiate from casuistics, which is the recording and study of cases and disease.

label: Retrospective Moral Judgment
summary: NLM MeSH describes Retrospective Moral Judgment as: The application of current standards of morality to past actions, institutions, or persons.

label: Wedge Argument
summary: NLM MeSH describes Wedge Argument as: An assertion that an action apparently unobjectionable in itself would set in motion a train of events leading ultimately to an undesirable outcome. (From Cambridge Dictionary of Philosophy, 1995)

label: Ethics Consultation
summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics Consultation as: Services provided by an individual ethicist ( ETHICISTS ) or an ethics team or committee ( ETHICS COMMITTEES, CLINICAL ) to address the ethical issues involved in a specific clinical case. The central purpose is to improve the process and outcomes of patients' care by helping to identify, analyze, and resolve ethical problems.

label: Professionalism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Professionalism as: The level of skill, good judgment, and polite behavior expected from people trained to do their jobs well.

label: Therapeutic Equipoise
summary: NLM MeSH describes Therapeutic Equipoise as: Expectation of real uncertainty on the part of the investigator regarding the comparative therapeutic merits of each arm in a trial.

label: Therapeutic Misconception
summary: NLM MeSH describes Therapeutic Misconception as: Misunderstanding among individuals, frequently research subjects, of scientific methods such as randomization and placebo controls.

label: Feminism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Feminism as: The theory of the political, economic, and social equality of the sexes and organized activity on behalf of women's rights and interests. (Webster New Collegiate Dictionary, 1981)

label: Beneficence
summary: NLM MeSH describes Beneficence as: The state or quality of being kind, charitable, or beneficial. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed). The ethical principle of BENEFICENCE requires producing net benefit over harm. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

label: Personal Autonomy
summary: NLM MeSH describes Personal Autonomy as: Self-directing freedom and especially moral independence. An ethical principle holds that the autonomy of persons ought to be respected. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

label: Social Justice
summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Justice as: An interactive process whereby members of a community are concerned for the equality and rights of all.

label: Environmental Justice
summary: NLM MeSH describes Environmental Justice as: The fair treatment and meaningful involvement of all people regardless of race, color, national origin, or income, with respect to the development, implementation, and enforcement of environmental laws, regulations, and policies. (www.epa.gov/environmentaljustice/learn-about-environmental-justice)

label: Moral Obligations
summary: NLM MeSH describes Moral Obligations as: Duties that are based in ETHICS , rather than in law.

label: Relational Autonomy
summary: NLM MeSH describes Relational Autonomy as: The social context within which all individuals exist and acknowledge the emotional and embodied aspects of decision-makers. The approach acknowledges the central role of others in decision-making, including clinicians, who have a responsibility to engage patients’ and surrogates’ emotional experiences.

label: Antiracism
summary: NLM MeSH describes Antiracism as: Beliefs, actions or intentions, and policies that oppose RACISM or discrimination based on RACE .

label: Biological and physical processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Biological and physical processes as: All continuing activities, functions, and phenomena associated with organisms and non-living matter. This category is also used for bioenergetic processes

label: Water properties
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water properties as: Measurable physical and chemical characteristics of water from different sources.

label: Natural resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Natural resources as: Stocks of anything naturally occurring that have a beneficial use for man including economic, nutritional, recreational, aesthetic, and other benefits.

label: Atmospheric and climatic processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric and climatic processes as: Phenomena affecting or occurring within the mass of gases that surrounds the earth, including its physics, chemistry, dynamics, and weather conditions. This category is also used for climate , microclimate , weather , with field inventory and monitoring for weather monitoring , and with field inventory and monitoring for weather observations

label: Coastal processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Coastal processes as: Processes unique to coastal areas including longshore transport, beach erosion, storm surge, shoreline change, delta formation, barrier island migration, beach stabilization by vegetation This category is also used with erosion for beach erosion , with erosion for coastal erosion , with hazards for coastal hazards , shoreline change , with erosion for shoreline erosion , and with erosion for shoreline retreat

label: Ecological processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ecological processes as: Dynamic biogeochemical interactions that occur among and between biotic and abiotic components of the biosphere. This category is also used for ecological models and environmental processes

label: Estuarine processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Estuarine processes as: Processes affecting estuaries including tides, waves, mixing of fluvial and marine waters This category is also used with sediment transport for estuarine sediment transport

label: Evolution
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Evolution as: Change in the genetic composition of populations of living organisms. This category is also used for gene flow

label: Fires
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Fires as: Combustion, marked by heat, light, flames, and often, smoke, caused by the natural or human-induced ignition of flammable materials. For fires set as part of natural resource management, use controlled fires. This category is also used with hazard preparedness for fire preparedness and fires (uncontrolled)

label: Geochemical processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geochemical processes as: Processes affecting the amount, distribution, or structure of chemical elements in air, water, soil, rocks, and minerals.

label: Geologic processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geologic processes as: All types of processes involving geological structures. This category is also used for lithification

label: Hydrocarbon reservoir processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Hydrocarbon reservoir processes as: Interactions among groundwater, hydrocarbons, and rock properties of subsurface geological formations, affecting the potential of those formations to form, trap, and permit the passage and extraction of hydrocarbons.

label: Impact cratering
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Impact cratering as: Impact of extraterrestrial objects such as asteroids, comets, and meteorites on Earth. This category is also used for asteroid impact , bolide impact , comet impact , and meteor impact

label: Ocean processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean processes as: Recurrent natural changes that are physical, biological, or chemical, actively affecting the seas and oceans. This category is also used with sediment transport for marine sediment transport , with hazards for ocean hazards , and with ocean characteristics for oceans

label: Physiological processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Physiological processes as: Characteristics and processes of individual organisms that are not the direct result of their interaction with other organisms or with the environment.

label: Dissolved gases
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Dissolved gases as: Gases such as ammonia, oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide in solution measured in a water sample.

label: Dissolved metals
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Dissolved metals as: Metal elements in solution, of concern in studies of hazards such as mine drainage and of water resource usability.

label: Dissolved organic compounds
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Dissolved organic compounds as: Organic compounds present in water, typically as anthropogenic contaminants including pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and herbicides.

label: Nutrient content (water)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Nutrient content (water) as: Contaminants in water that nourish organisms, especially plants. Includes nitrogen and phosphorus, either of which can lead to the harmful growth of algae and other plants when present to excess in a body of water. This category is also used for nitrogen content and phosphorus content

label: Oxygen content (water)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Oxygen content (water) as: Measurement of the concentration of oxygen dissolved in water, which is an important indicator of the condition of a water body. This category is also used for anoxia , dissolved oxygen , and hypoxia

label: Salinity
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Salinity as: Measure of the concentration of salts dissolved in a solution. This category is also used for chloride concentration

label: Sound velocity
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sound velocity as: Estimates of the velocity of sound in water, indexed by depth at a specific location, usually calculated from other water properties. This category is also used with profiles for sound velocity profiles

label: Suspended material (water)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Suspended material (water) as: Sediment or organic material carried in suspension in the water column, in contrast to material that moves on or near the bottom. May be measured directly by sampling, or indirectly by acoustic or optical backscatter or transmission. This category is also used for suspended sediment concentration and suspended-sediment concentration

label: Water column reflectivity
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water column reflectivity as: A measure of the strength of reflection from small particles suspended in water. It is usually measured by sending a pulse of sound or light through the water and measuring the sound or light that is returned. Water column reflectivity can be used to measure the concentration of suspended particles. This category is also used for backscatter (water column) , water column acoustic reflectivity , and water column optical reflectivity

label: Water hardness
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water hardness as: Indicator of the concentration of alkaline salts in water, mainly calcium and magnesium, as a measure of water quality. This category is also used for hardness (water)

label: Water pH
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water pH as: The negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration or activity of a water solution. Used for expressing both acidity (pH less than 7) and alkalinity (pH greater than 7), with 7 considered neutral. This category is also used for pH (water)

label: Water temperature
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water temperature as: The degrees of heat of water from a given source at a specific time. This category is also used for temperature (water)

label: Energy resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Energy resources as: Natural resources that are used for heat and power generation, including oil, natural gas, coal, and geothermal energy. This category is also used for energy sources and fossil fuels

label: Fishery resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Fishery resources as: The stock of anadromous, marine, and freshwater fish in fishing areas of commercial, subsistence, and recreational value.

label: Forest resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Forest resources as: Trees and associated vegetation available for human use. Use for timber and other forest resources with economic value. This category is also used for forestry

label: Mineral resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Mineral resources as: Natural occurrences of useful inorganic elements or compounds.

label: Soil resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil resources as: Natural resources of unconsolidated fragmented rock, humus, and mineral matter that cover the surface of the earth. This category is also used with contamination and pollution for soil pollution

label: Water resources
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water resources as: Stocks of water, the liquid derived from precipitation. A constituent of living matter and necessity for all life, it covers a large proportion of the earth's surface. This category is also used for hydrosphere and with contamination and pollution for water pollution

label: Atmospheric circulation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric circulation as: Movement of atmospheric gases around the earth.

label: Atmospheric deposition (chemical & particulate)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric deposition (chemical & particulate) as: The transfer of substances from the air to the surface of the earth, either in wet form (rain, fog, snow, dew, frost, hail) or in dry form (gases, aerosols, particles). This category is also used for atmospheric deposition (chemical and particulate) and atmospheric dust deposition

label: Climate change
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Climate change as: Long-term alteration in the characteristic weather conditions of a region, such as changes in precipitation and temperature. This category is also used for climate history , climate variability , climatic change , global climate change , global warming , and paleoclimate

label: Droughts
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Droughts as: Extended periods of moisture deficit over a sizeable area sufficient to have an adverse effect on vegetation, animals, or man. This category is also used for drought

label: Evaporation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Evaporation as: Transfer of water from a surface into the atmosphere. This category is also used with transpiration for evapotranspiration

label: Greenhouse effect
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Greenhouse effect as: Local, regional, or global warming in the atmosphere due to the higher heat capacity of certain gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, and ozone.

label: Ocean-atmosphere interaction
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean-atmosphere interaction as: Processes, including momentum, heat, gas and other exchanges, which result in profound effects on climate and interactions between the air in the lowest part of the atmosphere and the oceans. This category is also used for El Nino and La Nina

label: Precipitation (atmospheric)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Precipitation (atmospheric) as: Any or all forms of water particles that fall from the atmosphere, such as rain, snow, hail and sleet. This category is also used with field inventory and monitoring for precipitation measurement , rain , rainfall , with field inventory and monitoring for rainfall measurement , snow , snowfall , and with field inventory and monitoring for snowfall measurement

label: Storms
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Storms as: Atmospheric disturbances with winds of unusual force or direction. Accompanied by rain, snow, hail, or sleet, and often by thunder and lightning.

label: Wind
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Wind as: Local air movements. This category is also used with erosion for wind erosion

label: Barrier island migration
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Barrier island migration as: The slow, landward movement of barrier islands in response to sea level rise and repeated storm washover.

label: Coastal emergence
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Coastal emergence as: Relative uplift of the coast accompanied by seaward displacement of the shoreline. This category is also used for regression (marine)

label: Coastal submergence
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Coastal submergence as: Relative subsidence of the coast accompanied by landward displacement of the shoreline. This category is also used for transgression (marine)

label: Longshore currents
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Longshore currents as: Movement of water parallel to the coast due to waves striking the shoreline at an angle This category is also used with sediment transport for littoral drift and with sediment transport for longshore drift

label: Shoreline accretion
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Shoreline accretion as: Seaward migration of the shoreline resulting from the addition of earth materials.

label: Tidal currents
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Tidal currents as: Currents caused by tidal changes in water level from one body of water to another.

label: Algal blooms
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Algal blooms as: Exceptional growth of algae and cyanobacteria in lakes, rivers or oceans due to excessive nutrients or climatic conditions. This category is also used for brown tides , with hazards for harmful algal blooms , and red tides

label: Bioaccumulation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Bioaccumulation as: The biological sequestering of a substance at a higher concentration than that at which it occurs in the surrounding environment or medium. Also, the process whereby a substance enters an organism through the gills, epithelial tissues, dietary, or other sources. This category is also used for bioconcentration

label: Biogeochemical cycling
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Biogeochemical cycling as: The cycling of chemical constituents through a biological system. This category is also used for biogeochemical functioning , biogeochemical processes , decomposition (organic) , and organic decomposition

label: Biological productivity
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Biological productivity as: The rate at which primary producers in the ecosystem utilize solar energy to produce food for consumption by other organisms. Do not use this term for productivity of organisms related to studies of the reproduction rates of a species.

label: Carbon flux
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Carbon flux as: The rate and amount of carbon exchanged between the oceans, atmosphere, land, and living things. This category is also used for carbon exchange

label: Contaminant transport
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Contaminant transport as: Processes involved in the movement of impurities through air, water, and soil.

label: Dispersal (organisms)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Dispersal (organisms) as: The dissemination or geographic spread of individuals of a plant or animal population. This category is also used for colonization (organisms)

label: Ecological competition
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ecological competition as: The struggle between members of two or more species for scarce environmental resources.

label: Ecosystem functions
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ecosystem functions as: The total life activities of organisms in habitats and the effects of those activities on the nonliving components of the environment. This category is also used with estuarine ecosystems for estuarine ecosystem functions

label: Ecosystem resilience
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ecosystem resilience as: Measure of the persistence of systems and of their ability to absorb change and disturbance and still maintain the same relationships between populations or state variables. (Holling, 1973) This category is also used for ecological resilience

label: Eutrophication
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Eutrophication as: The process by which water becomes enriched with plant nutrients, most commonly phosphorus and nitrogen.

label: Extinction and extirpation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Extinction and extirpation as: Extinction is the complete disappearance of a species from the earth. Extirpation is the complete disappearance (elimination) of a species from a given region, island, or area. This category is also used for extirpation

label: Habitat alteration and disturbance
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Habitat alteration and disturbance as: Changes in the environments where plants and animals live. Includes natural changes as well as results of human actions, deliberate or accidental. This category is also used for ecological disturbance , environmental disturbance , habitat destruction , and habitat disturbance

label: Migration (organisms)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Migration (organisms) as: The movement of animals, often periodical, from one area to another due to seasonal changes, availability of food, or climatic conditions. This category is also used with invasive species for biological invasions , with biogeography for flyways , and seasonal migration

label: Pollination
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Pollination as: Wind, bees, or other agents transfer plant pollen from flower anthers or cones to stigmas, thereby fertilizing plants for reproduction.

label: Succession (biological)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Succession (biological) as: Gradual replacement of one species in an area by another. This category is also used for ecologic succession

label: Transpiration
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Transpiration as: Evaporation of water from plants. This category is also used with evaporation for evapotranspiration

label: Estuarine currents
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Estuarine currents as: Movement of water within estuaries due to the complex interaction of winds, tides, and variations in water density

label: Estuarine mixing
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Estuarine mixing as: Interaction of tidal forcing and river discharge in an estuary, leading to any of three vertical salinity profiles: salt wedge, stratified, or well mixed. We also include mixing due to extreme events such as storm surge.

label: Wildfires
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Wildfires as: Uncontrolled fires that originate as a result of natural phenomena or human activities in natural areas such as forests, grasslands, or shrub lands, but may also spread to structures and human-occupied environments. This category is also used for wildland fire

label: Biodegradation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Biodegradation as: Reduction in the concentration of harmful chemicals by the action of animals and plants. This category is also used for natural attenuation (harmful chemicals)

label: Carbon sequestration
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Carbon sequestration as: Long-term storage of carbon in soils and terrestrial organic material, either by natural or engineered processes. Typically of importance for the balance of CO2 in the global climate system. This category is also used for carbon capture , carbon capture and storage , and carbon storage

label: Ocean acidification
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean acidification as: Decrease in the pH of ocean waters as a result of the increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration.

label: Ore formation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ore formation as: Geochemical processes resulting in concentration of useful chemical elements and compounds, in earth materials. Typically refers to metal ores. This category is also used for metallogenesis , metallogeny , and mineralization

label: Oxidation and reduction
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Oxidation and reduction as: Addition or reduction of oxygen in a compound accompanied by exchange of electrons among atoms. This category is also used for fermentation

label: Reaction transport
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Reaction transport as: Chemical reactions occurring during ground-water flow.

label: Sorption
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sorption as: Attachment of chemical substances to materials, either externally (by adsorption) or internally (by absorption). This category is also used for absorption and adsorption

label: Thermal maturation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Thermal maturation as: Chemical alteration of organic material within sediments and sedimentary rocks as a result of heat. Measures of thermal maturation indicate the extent of transformation of detrital organic material into coal and petroleum. This category is also used for thermal indices , thermal maturity , and vitrinite reflectance

label: Deformation (geologic)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Deformation (geologic) as: Change in form and structure of geologic materials in response to stress, typically heat and pressure. This category is also used for rheology and strain history

label: Diagenesis
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Diagenesis as: Chemical, physical, and biological changes in sediment during and after its conversion to rock (lithification).

label: Earth tides
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth tides as: Periodic changes in the earth surface topography caused by the gravitational attraction of the moon and sun, measured with tiltmeters. Used in studies of volcanic activity.

label: Earthquakes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earthquakes as: Ground shaking caused by the sudden release of accumulated strain by an abrupt shift of rock along a fracture in the earth or by volcanic or magmatic activity, or other sudden stress changes in the earth. This category is also used with hazards for earthquake hazards

label: Erosion
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Erosion as: The process whereby materials of the earth's crust are loosened, dissolved, or worn away and simultaneously moved from one place to another. This category is also used with coastal processes for beach erosion , with coastal processes for coastal erosion , dissolution , with coastal processes for shoreline erosion , with coastal processes for shoreline retreat , and with wind for wind erosion

label: Fluid migration
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Fluid migration as: Movement or migration of fluids, including petroleum and other chemicals through earth materials by natural or anthropogenic forces. This category is also used for interstitial fluid and pore fluid

label: Glaciation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Glaciation as: The geologic processes involved in the formation, movement, changes, and effects of large ice masses (glaciers).

label: Heat flow (earth)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Heat flow (earth) as: Energy transferred by a difference in temperature through the surface of the earth. This category is also used for geothermics and heatflow (earth)

label: Hydrothermal processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Hydrothermal processes as: Natural phenomena relating to heated water generated by igneous activity.

label: Isostasy
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Isostasy as: Condition of equilibrium or buoyancy of the earth's crust above the mantle.

label: Magnetic storms
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Magnetic storms as: A period of time during which the earth's magnetic field varies rapidly. During magnetic storms, satellite electronics can be damaged through the build up and subsequent discharge of static electric charges and astronauts and high-altitude pilots can be subjected to increased levels of radiation. This category is also used for geomagnetic storms

label: Metamorphism (geological)
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Metamorphism (geological) as: Process by which rocks are altered in composition and texture by extreme heat, high pressure, or the action of chemicals.

label: Sediment transport
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sediment transport as: Transport of solid particles of unconsolidated rock and mineral fragments, chemical precipitates, or biological materials. This category is also used for alluvial transport , bed load , bedload , density flow , dust transport , with estuarine processes for estuarine sediment transport , with longshore currents for littoral drift , with longshore currents for longshore drift , with ocean processes for marine sediment transport , suspended load , and turbidity flow

label: Sedimentation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sedimentation as: Process of deposition of sediments (loose, uncemented pieces of rock, mineral fragments, or biological materials). The sediments settle out of water or air into layers on a surface. This category is also used for alluvial sedimentation , deposition (sediment) , and dust deposition

label: Slope processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Slope processes as: The down slope movement of earth material under the influence of gravity. This category is also used for mass wasting and soil creep

label: Soil formation
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil formation as: Geological, geochemical, and ecological processes that work together to produce soils. This category is also used for pedogenesis

label: Subsidence
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Subsidence as: Settling, compaction, or caving in of land caused by subsurface mining, ground-water withdrawal, or pumping of oil and gas. This category is also used for land subsidence and with maps and atlases for land subsidence maps

label: Tectonic processes
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Tectonic processes as: The structural forces affecting the deformation, uplift, and movement of the earth's crust. This category is also used for continental drift , dynamic geology , with maps and atlases for paleotectonic maps , plate tectonics , subduction , with maps and atlases for tectonic maps , tectonics , and wilson cycle

label: Uplift
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Uplift as: Local or regional rise in the elevation of the land surface, usually due to tectonic or volcanic processes.

label: Volcanic activity
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Volcanic activity as: Episodes during which gases, ash, and lava (molten rock) escape from vents in the earth's crust, accompanied by minor tremors. This category is also used for eruption , lava flows , pyroclastic flows , volcanic tremors , volcanism , and with field inventory and monitoring for volcano monitoring

label: Floods
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Floods as: Relatively high water that overflows the natural or artificial banks of a stream or coastal area that submerges land not normally below water level. This category is also used for bankfull stage and with hazard preparedness for flood preparedness

label: Groundwater and surface-water interaction
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Groundwater and surface-water interaction as: Traditionally, management of water resources has focused on surface water or groundwater as if they were separate entities. As development of land and water resources increases, it is apparent that development of either of these resources affects the quantity and quality of the other. Nearly all surface-water features (streams, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands, and estuaries) interact with groundwater. These interactions take many forms. In many situations, surface-water bodies gain water and solutes from groundwater systems and in others the surface-water body is a source of groundwater recharge and causes changes in groundwater quality. As a result, withdrawal of water from streams can deplete groundwater or conversely, pumpage of groundwater can deplete water in streams, lakes, or wetlands. Pollution of surface water can cause degradation of groundwater quality and conversely pollution of groundwater can degrade surface water. This category is also used for aquifer-surface water interaction , ground-water/surface-water interaction , groundwater/surface water interaction , hyporheic zone processes , surface water/groundwater interaction , and surface-water/ground-water interaction

label: Groundwater flow
summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Groundwater flow as: Movement of subsurface water in the saturated zone from areas of recharge to areas of discharge. This category is also used for ground-water flow , groundwater flow modeling , and groundwater movement
